source_text: Ἡ πρόσκλαυσις ἔξω τῆς πύλης τοῦ εὐκτηρίου ἐστίν, ἔνθα ἑστῶτα τὸν ἁμαρτόντα, χρὴ τῶν εἰσιόντων δεῖσθαι πιστῶν, ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ εὔχεσθαι. Ἡ ἀκρόασις ἔνδοθι τῆς πύλης ἐν τῷ νάρθηκι, ἔνθα ἑστάναι χρὴ τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα ἕως τῶν κατηχουμένων, καὶ ἐντεῦθεν ἐξέρχεσθαι, ἀκούων γάρ, φησί, τῶν Γραφῶν καὶ τῆς διδασκαλίας, ἐκβαλλέσθω καὶ μὴ ἀξιούσθω προσευχῆς. Ἡ δὲ ὑπόπτωσις, ἵνα ἔσωθεν τῆς πύλης τοῦ ναοῦ ἱστάμενος, μετὰ τῶν κατηχουμένων ἐξέρχηται· ἡ σύστασις ἵνα συνίσταται τοῖς πιστοῖς καὶ μὴ ἐξέρχηται μετὰ τῶν κατηχουμένων. Τελευταῖον, ἡ μέθεξις τῶν ἁγιασμάτων.
thought_title: Penitential stations and the final goal of the mysteries
orientation: Gregory lists the ordered places where a penitent stands — outside the gate of the prayer house, inside the gate in the narthex, within the gate of the temple, admitted to the faithful, and finally sharing in the holy mysteries — marking each stage by where the person stands and whether they leave with the catechumens or stay with the faithful.
pass_a_gloss: The prostration is outside the gate of the prayer house, where the one who sinned must stand, and it is necessary that those entering ask the faithful to pray for him. The hearing is inside the gate in the narthex, where the one who has sinned must stand until the catechumens, and from there go out, for hearing the Scriptures and the teaching, let him be cast out and not be counted worthy of prayer. The falling-prostrate, so that standing from within the gate of the temple he may go out with the catechumens. The standing-together, so that he may be introduced to the faithful and not go out with the catechumens. Finally, the sharing of the holy things.

lemmas.gloss: prostration, act of throwing oneself down in penitence
hearing, the station of hearing Scripture
falling prostrate, a deeper penitential posture
standing together, introduction to full fellowship

choices.why: The Greek noun denotes the act of throwing oneself down before the gate; 'prostration' is the standard term for this penitential station.
Glossary sense: place of prayer; the brief uses 'prayers' for εὐχαί, so 'prayer house' keeps the same root.
Refers to the station where the penitent hears Scripture and teaching; 'hearing' matches the literal sense of ἀκρόασις.
A distinct, lower posture than πρόσκλαυσις; the compound ὑπό-πτωσις implies falling under/forward.
Literal sense of σύν-στασις; the penitent now stands with the faithful instead of leaving with the catechumens.
Glossary maps ἁγιασμάτων to 'holy things, mysteries, the Eucharist'; μέθεξις is sharing/participation.

pass_b_english: The weeping takes place outside the gate of the prayer house, where the one who has sinned must stand and beg the faithful as they enter to pray for him. The hearing takes place inside the gate in the narthex, where the one who has sinned must stand until the catechumens depart, and from there he must leave, for 'hearing the Scriptures and the teaching, let him be put out and not be deemed worthy of prayer.' The falling prostrate means he stands inside the gate of the sanctuary and leaves with the catechumens. The standing together means he stands with the faithful and does not leave with the catechumens. Last of all comes the sharing of the holy things.

problems.quote: The prostration takes place outside the gate
problems.why: πρόσκλαυσις means weeping or mourning, not prostration. Calling it prostration confuses this first stage with the later ὑπόπτωσις.
problems.fix: The weeping takes place outside the gate of the prayer house

edits.old: The prostration takes place outside the gate
edits.new: The weeping takes place outside the gate

fixed: Fixed mistranslation: source πρόσκλαυσις is weeping, distinct from later ὑπόπτωσις (falling prostrate).

problems.quote: he is introduced to the faithful
problems.why: Here συνίσταται means to stand together with the faithful, which gives this stage its name ('standing together'). 'Introduced' is the wrong sense of the word and hides the meaning.
problems.fix: The standing together means he stands with the faithful and does not leave with the catechumens.
problems.ruling: σύστασις named from συνίσταται τοῖς πιστοῖς: stand with faithful, not merely be introduced.

edits.old: he is introduced to the faithful

fixed: Fixed `he is introduced to the faithful` -> `he stands with the faithful`: συνίσταται τοῖς πιστοῖς means stands with the faithful, matching σύστασις as standing together.

problems.quote: where the one who has sinned stands while those entering ask the faithful to pray for him
problems.source_quote: ἔνθα ἑστῶτα τὸν ἁμαρτόντα, χρὴ τῶν εἰσιόντων δεῖσθαι πιστῶν, ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ εὔχεσθαι
problems.why: In the source, the sinner must beg the faithful who are entering to pray for him. The English makes the people entering do the asking and also drops the obligation.
problems.fix: where the one who has sinned must stand and beg the faithful as they enter to pray for him.
problems.ruling: χρὴ … δεῖσθαι τῶν εἰσιόντων πιστῶν: sinner must beg entering faithful; English has entrants ask other faithful, dropping χρὴ.

edits.old: where the one who has sinned stands while those entering ask the faithful to pray for him
edits.new: where the one who has sinned must stand and beg the faithful as they enter to pray for him

fixed: agency: fixed — source has accusative sinner as subject (τὸν ἁμαρτόντα / ἑστῶτα) begging (δεῖσθαι) the entering faithful (τῶν εἰσιόντων πιστῶν); English had reversed the agency.
